rules.title: Security deposit cap of 1.5 months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent, and pet deposits count toward the cap.

exemption_conditions.condition: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt (unless the tenant opts in by written request)
Owner-occupied dwellings with three or fewer units

coverage.notes: A tenant in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling may make the law applicable 30 days after sending the landlord a written request.

rules.coverage_text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the law applicable by written request (effective 30 days later).
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days of tenancy termination
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after a tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions sent by registered or certified mail; if tenants are displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation, the deposit must be returned within five business days. Wrongful withholding exposes the landlord to double damages.

exemption_conditions.condition: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt from the Security Deposit Law unless the tenant opts in

coverage.notes: If tenant breaks lease without cause, the 30 days start when unit is re-rented or the lease expires, whichever first.

rules.coverage_text: Applies to most residential rental properties covered by the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span:
Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security 
deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Security deposit return after domestic violence lease termination
rules.requirement: When a tenant terminates a lease under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must make the security deposit plus interest available within 15 business days and notify the tenant in writing within three business days of where and when to pick it up.

exemption_conditions.condition: Does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals

coverage.notes: Applies to tenants terminating leases early as victims of domestic violence.

rules.coverage_text: Tenants who terminate a lease early under the Safe Housing Act as domestic violence victims.
rules.quoted_span:
Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available 
the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s 
agent.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the statutory good causes (e.g., nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, rule violations, unconscionable-increase refusal, retirement from residential use, condo conversion, owner occupancy in small buildings, drug or assault convictions).

exemption_conditions.condition: Two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units may be exempt
Owner-occupied premises with three or fewer units
Hotel, motel, or guest house rented to transient guests or seasonal tenants (unless occupant has no alternate residence and lives there continually)
Unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies it
exemption_conditions.value: unit held in trust for developmentally disabled family member

coverage.notes: Hotel and motel guests are covered if they have no alternate residence and reside there continually.

rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile home park land, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; transient hotel/motel/guest house guests and seasonal tenants; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

rules.title: Senior citizen and disabled protected tenancy in conversions
rules.requirement: Eligible senior citizens, permanently disabled tenants and certain disabled veterans in buildings being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their income meets the statutory limit.

property_types_covered: buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership
coverage.notes: Tenant must be 62+ before conversion recording, permanently disabled, or a qualifying disabled veteran, have lived in the building at least one year before conversion recording, and have family income not more than 3x county per capita income or $50,000, whichever is greater.

rules.coverage_text: Qualifying senior citizens, disabled tenants and disabled veterans living in buildings being converted for at least one year before the conversion recording date, subject to income limits.
citation_aliases: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.quoted_span:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years 
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their 
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).

rules.title: Rent increases must not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal rent ordinance; a tenant can be evicted for not paying an increase only after a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. The state itself sets no rent control cap.

coverage.notes: Applies in context of eviction for nonpayment of rent increase under the Anti-Eviction Act.

rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.interaction: Increases must also comply with municipal rent control ordinances where they exist.
rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.

rules.title: No rent increases to cover conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion; this applies to all tenants in the building.

property_types_covered: buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership
coverage.notes: Applies to all tenants in the building regardless of protected tenancy eligibility; increases for new services or amenities are allowed.

rules.coverage_text: All tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership.
rules.exemptions: Increases to cover new services or amenities are not prohibited.
rules.quoted_span:
If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee 
simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

rules.title: New construction exempt from local rent control for 30 years
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinance for 30 years following completion of construction.

coverage.notes: Exemption lasts 30 years from completion of construction.

rules.coverage_text: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, for 30 years after completion of construction.
rules.interaction: State law preempts application of local rent control ordinances to newly constructed multiple dwellings for 30 years.
rules.quoted_span:
Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

rules.title: LAD ban on source of lawful income discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in renting housing based on, among other characteristics, the applicant's source of lawful income.

exemption_conditions.condition: Rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home; residences exclusively for one sex

coverage.notes: Exemptions per N.J.S.A. 10:5-5(n); age-restricted housing exemption pertains to familial status.

rules.coverage_text: All landlord-tenant relationships, with listed exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for one sex; age-restricted housing as to familial status.
rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.

llm.notes: The document is the NJ DCA Truth in Renting guide. I took rules only from the content it describes. The guide says New Jersey has no state rent control. It also says landlords may charge for credit reports and reasonable application fees, but cites no state law setting a cap, so I did not record that as an application_screening_fees rule. It contains no rules on algorithmic rent setting.
